You can send one test per rule every 10 seconds. A test message's text starts with 🧪 Test from Picto and ends with "Nothing has fired.", and the payload has "test": true. A test doesn't change the rule's Last fired time or delivery status.

Picto checks every turned-on rule once a minute. It counts the rule's signal for the client app over the last window, by the time each signal reached the server. When the count is at least the threshold, the rule fires. After a rule fires, it doesn't fire again until a full window has passed. A 5-minute rule that keeps breaching fires at most once every 5 minutes. A failed delivery isn't retried; the rule waits the same window. The rule's row shows Last fired (or Never) with a delivered or failed badge. Hover over a failed badge to see the error, such as the HTTP status and response body.

A fired alert is a POST with Content-Type: application/json. This body is what a Frozen frames rule with a threshold of 5 and a 5-minute window sends: { "text": "🚨 jank_events: 7 in the last 300s (threshold: 5)", "metricType": "jank_events", "count": 7, "threshold": 5, "windowSeconds": 300, "clientAppId": " ", "organizationId": " ", "firedAt": "2026-11-13T09:41:00.000" } Field Meaning text A ready-to-show summary metricType exceptions, jank_events (frozen frames) or tap_cluster_events (frustration taps) count How many were counted in the window. Counting stops once the threshold is met, so above 500 this can be lower than the true number. threshold The rule's threshold windowSeconds The rule's window, in seconds clientAppId, organizationId Which client app and organization the rule belongs to firedAt When the rule fired, as an ISO 8601 timestamp

s.h: Change, pause or delete a rule
s.b: Each action is a button on the rule's row: Edit opens the same form. Click Save changes. Disable turns the rule off, and Enable turns it back on. The Status column shows on or off. A rule that's off isn't checked. The trash button deletes the rule after you confirm. This can't be undone. Deleting the client app or the organization deletes its rules too.

docs.d: Accounts, organizations, apps, API keys and collaborators.

s.b: Your dashboard account owns organizations, each organization holds client apps, and each client app has the API key your app records with. An organization groups client apps and the people who can see them. A client app is one app, or one build you want to record separately. Every session belongs to a client app.

Go to picto.dev/sign-up, enter Your name and Work email, and click Send my sign-in link. Open the emailed link to finish. There's no password to choose. The account starts with no organization. The dashboard's Get started page walks you through naming your organization and first client app and choosing a plan (see Plans & Retention). Sign-up refuses two kinds of address: An address with a + in it: "Email aliases (addresses with a "+" in them) are not accepted. Sign up with your main address instead." An address that reaches an inbox that already has an account: "An account already exists for this inbox. Sign in with the address you first signed up with instead." For Gmail, dots in the name and googlemail.com reach the same inbox.

An invite link looks like https://picto.dev/join?t= . Open it, enter Your name and Work email, and open the sign-in link Picto emails you. Redeeming an invite creates your account with an organization named after you, a client app called My app, and a 14-day trial that starts when you redeem it. The link is refused when it: Was revoked: "That invite link is not valid. It may have been revoked — ask whoever sent it for a new one." Was already used: "That invite link has already been used to create an account. Sign in instead, or ask for a new invite." Is more than 14 days old: "That invite link has expired. Ask whoever sent it for a new one."

Go to /sign-in, enter your Email, and click Email me a sign-in link. To use a password, click Sign in with a password instead. An account has no password until you add one: open Account in the sidebar, find Password under Sign-in, and click Add a password. If you forget it, click Forgot password? on the sign-in page and then Send reset link. A reset link works for ten minutes.

To create one, open the organization switcher in the top bar, choose New organization, enter the Organization name and click Create organization. You're its owner. To rename one, open Organization in the sidebar, edit Name and click Save. Only the owner can. To delete one, open Organization and click Delete organization under Danger zone, then confirm. This deletes every client app, recording and signal in it, and can't be undone. If the organization has a paid plan, Picto cancels it first so it isn't charged again. If that cancellation fails, nothing is deleted.

To create one, open the app switcher in the top bar, choose New app, enter the App name and click Create app. Only the organization's owner sees New app. To rename one, open App settings, edit Name under App and click Save. To delete one, open App settings and click Delete app under Danger zone, then confirm. This deletes every recording, exception and signal that belongs to it, and can't be undone.

Your app authenticates every upload with the client app's API key. Open App settings. The API key section shows the key masked: click Reveal key to see it, or Copy key to copy it without showing it. See Quick Start for where the key goes. To replace the key, click Regenerate key under Danger zone and confirm. Only the owner can. The old key stops working at once, and builds that still use it can't upload until you ship the new one.

s.h: Set the sampling rate and upload tokens
s.b: App settings also holds Sampling rate, the share of app runs Picto records. See Sampling. Account also holds Upload tokens, which picto:upload_assets uses. See Uploading Assets.

1. Open Organization in the sidebar. 2. Under Collaborators, enter their email in Invite a collaborator. 3. Click Send invite. Picto emails them an invite. They don't need an account yet: they get access when they sign up with that address. The address is matched without regard to letter case. Collaborators see the organization's client apps, sessions, signals and alert rules, can copy API keys, and can delete recordings. Only the owner can: Invite or remove collaborators. Create, rename or delete client apps, change the sampling rate, and regenerate API keys. Create alert rules (see Alerts). Rename, transfer or delete the organization, and manage its plan. To remove a collaborator, click Remove collaborator next to their email and confirm.

Under Ownership on the Organization page, click Make owner next to a collaborator, then Transfer ownership. The new owner controls billing, and the client apps and alert rules you own in the organization move to them. You stay on as a collaborator, and only the new owner can hand it back. If there's nobody to pick, the section says No eligible collaborators. Invite someone first.
As a collaborator, open Organization and click Leave organization, then Leave. You lose access until you're invited again. An owner can't leave; transfer ownership first.

1. Open Account and click Delete account under Danger zone. 2. Read the list of what will go. Every organization you own is deleted with everything in it, and you leave the ones you only collaborate on. 3. Type the confirmation phrase shown in Type "…" to confirm: the name of your first owned organization, or your email if you own none. 4. If your account has a password, enter it in Your current password and click Delete my account. If it doesn't, click Email me a confirmation link and open the link within one hour. Any paid plan is cancelled first. If that fails, nothing is deleted. Once confirmed, deletion is immediate and nothing can be restored.

docs.d: Session limits, billing and how long recordings are kept.

s.b: Plans differ only in how many sessions an organization can record each billing period; every plan has the whole dashboard, and every recording is kept for 30 days.

Each organization has its own plan. The organization's owner picks one from Get started or the Plan section of the Organization page. Plan Price Sessions included per period Overage buffer Starter $49 / month 2,500 1,000 Growth $149 / month 10,000 2,500 Scale $399 / month 40,000 10,000 Enterprise Custom Custom Custom The overage buffer is extra sessions on top of the included ones, so a busy week keeps recording. Agent access is on every plan, with hourly limits that rise with the plan (see Sessions CLI & MCP). Enterprise is arranged through picto.dev/enterprise.

A session is one run of your app that you record and upload, however long it lasts. Sessions are counted across every client app in the organization. A session is counted once, in the billing period its first segment was uploaded in. Later segments of the same session don't count again, even when they arrive in the next period. Watching replays costs nothing. See How Sessions Work for segments. The count is updated about once a minute, and within a period it never goes down. A session that ages out of retention after it was counted stays counted.

Uploads keep working until the period's count passes the included sessions plus the overage buffer. After that, Picto refuses new sessions until you upgrade or the next billing period starts. Segments of a session that was already counted still upload. Refused sessions stay queued on the device and upload once uploads are allowed again. See Troubleshooting for what the SDK reports. The server refuses an upload with one of these messages: Message Cause "This organization has used its plan's sessions plus its -session overage buffer for this billing period. Upgrade your plan, or wait for the next billing period, to resume uploads." The period's sessions passed the included sessions plus the buffer. "This organization's subscription is not active (status: )." Payment is overdue or unpaid, billing is paused, or a cancelled plan reached its period end. "This organization has no active subscription. Uploads are disabled until you subscribe to a plan." The organization has never had a plan, or its invite trial ended. The Plan and usage section of the Organization page shows the period's usage against the plan and how much buffer is left.

The Plan and usage section shows the plan's status as a badge: Status Uploads What it means Active Allowed The plan renews on the date shown. On trial Allowed The first payment is on the date shown. Cancelled Allowed until the period ends Recording continues until the period end, then uploads stop. Payment overdue Stopped The last payment didn't go through. Unpaid Stopped Payment didn't go through. Paused Stopped Billing is paused. Ended, Expired Stopped The plan has ended. Choose a plan to record again. When uploads stop, nothing already recorded is deleted.

On the Organization page, click Manage billing to open the billing portal. There you can move up or down a plan, update your payment method, or cancel. A cancelled plan keeps working until the end of the period you paid for. Only the organization's owner sees the Plan section. Deleting the organization cancels its plan first (see Account & Team).

An organization created by redeeming an invite can upload for 14 days from the moment the invite was redeemed, with no plan. When the trial ends, uploads stop with the "no active subscription" message until the owner chooses a plan. Everything recorded during the trial stays.

A recording is deleted 30 days after it reached the server, not 30 days after the device recorded it. The deletion job runs once a day, so a recording can last up to a day past 30 days. Watching a replay doesn't extend it. Retention is the same on every plan and can't be changed. What's deleted after 30 days: The replay and its segments. The session's row in the Sessions list, with its metadata, tags and user ID. What stays: Exceptions, frozen frames and frustration taps, in their own lists. Opening one whose replay is gone reports that the recording is missing. Organizations, client apps, API keys, collaborators, alert rules and uploaded assets. Deleting a client app or an organization removes its recordings at once, without waiting for the 30 days.

Save it before it's deleted. dart run picto:sessions download writes a session's raw recording bytes to a file, and video and frames render it to an .mp4 or PNG stills. See Sessions CLI & MCP. The following command saves a session's recording to a local file. Add --sequence for a session with more than one segment. dart run picto:sessions download 3f9c2a7e -o 3f9c2a7e.bin

docs.d: The picto:sessions CLI and the picto:mcp server.

s.b: dart run picto:sessions and dart run picto:mcp give a coding agent read access to your recorded sessions, so it can see what a user did instead of guessing. Both ship in the picto package, so any project that depends on it has them. They read exactly what your account can see in the dashboard, and never change anything.

You need: A project that depends on picto (see Quick Start). A Picto account with a password. An account made from a sign-in link has none: open Account in the dashboard and click Add a password (see Account & Team). An organization with a plan or a running invite trial. Agent access is on every plan.

Run login once in a terminal: dart run picto:sessions login It asks for your email and password (the password isn't echoed) and saves the session to ~/.config/picto/credentials.json, readable only by you. $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/picto is used instead when that variable is set. Pass --email to skip the first prompt. --password also exists, but the prompt keeps your password out of your shell history. The saved session renews itself while it's in use, so it lasts as long as a picto:sessions command runs at least once a week. Once it lapses, every command exits with code 3 and says to run dart run picto:sessions login. logout ends the session on the server as well as removing it from your machine: dart run picto:sessions logout For CI, pass --token or set PICTO_TOKEN to use a bearer token instead of the saved session. Nothing is saved or renewed.

Every command except login, logout and list takes a session ID, as list prints it. Command What it does list Recent sessions, newest first show One session: its segments, metadata, and every exception, tap cluster and frozen frame with its time in the session timeline Every event in the session in order, each with its session time. No images, so it's the fastest way to read a session. video Renders an .mp4, with a .manifest.json and a .captions.vtt beside it frames Renders PNG stills into a directory, with a manifest.json download Saves one segment's raw recording bytes timeline, video and frames render on Picto's servers and wait for the result, for up to 10 minutes. Rendered files stay on the server for 24 hours.

Option Default Effect --limit 20 Sessions per page --before None The next page. A page that has more prints the cursor (nextBefore in JSON). --has-errors None Only sessions with an exception --has-rage-taps None Only sessions with a rage tap --platform None Only ios, android, macos or web --client-app None Only one client app

s.h: Options for timeline, video and frames
s.b: Option Default Effect --start , --end Whole session A window in session time: 1:03, 63s or 63000 (milliseconds) --keep-idle Off Keep idle stretches (see Idle stretches are cut) --max-width 720 Downscale frames to at most this width --no-pointers Off Don't draw tap ripples video also takes -o, --output (default picto- .mp4) and --fps , 1 to 30 (default 10). frames also takes -o, --output (default picto- -frames), --every for the periodic frames (default 1s), and --no-event-frames to drop the extra frame it otherwise takes at each tap, screen change and error.
download takes -o, --output (default picto- - .bin) and --sequence . A session with more than one segment needs --sequence; without it the command fails with a message listing the segment numbers.

On a terminal the commands print tables and summaries. When stdout isn't a terminal, which is how an agent's shell tool runs them, they print JSON. --json forces JSON anywhere. Failures are JSON too, under an error key with exitCode and message, and the exit code tells an agent what to do next: Exit code Meaning 0 Success 1 Something failed. The message says what, including an hourly limit or a failed render. 2 The command was used wrongly 3 Not signed in, the session expired, or access was refused. Sign in again. 4 No such session, or not one this account can see 5 The session's organization has no plan or invite trial. The error has code: "plan_required" and an upgradeUrl. Signing in again won't help; choosing a plan will.

If your agent speaks MCP, dart run picto:mcp offers the same commands as tools, over stdio. It uses the saved sign-in and never asks for a password, so run dart run picto:sessions login in a terminal first. For Claude Code, run this from your app's project directory, the one whose pubspec.yaml depends on picto: claude mcp add picto -- dart run picto:mcp Most other clients read an mcp.json like the following. dart run picto:mcp has to start inside a project that depends on picto, so set cwd to your app's directory: { "mcpServers": { "picto": { "command": "dart", "args": ["run", "picto:mcp"], "cwd": "/path/to/your/app" } } } If your client has no cwd setting, use "command": "sh" with "args": ["-c", "cd /path/to/your/app && dart run picto:mcp"]. The tools mirror the commands: Tool Same as Parameters list_sessions list limit, before, has_errors, has_rage_taps, platform, client_app_id get_session show session_id get_timeline timeline session_id, start, end, keep_idle render_video video session_id, start, end, keep_idle, output, fps, max_width, pointers render_frames frames session_id, start, end, keep_idle, output, every, event_frames, max_width, pointers, include_images, image_max_widt

timeline, video and frames skip idle stretches by default, the same way the dashboard's Skip idle does: any quiet gap longer than 5 seconds is cut down to its first 5 seconds. The blank stretch before the app's first paint is always cut, even with --keep-idle. Because cuts make output time differ from session time, every render says so: A note on stderr, and as idleNote in the JSON result, says how many stretches were cut and how much time they covered. The manifest lists each cut under idle.skipped with its start, end and reason (idle or before_first_paint), and idle.savedMs totals them. segments maps output time back to session time. Every event in the manifest has a sessionMs and an outputMs. outputMs is null for an event inside a cut. captions.vtt has a cue at each cut, so a model watching the video sees it too. When an agent quotes a time back to you, it should use sessionMs, which matches the dashboard's replay timeline. A render that would be too long, or produce too many frames, fails with a message saying to narrow the window with --start and --end. A window that was entirely idle fails too, and the message says to re-run with --keep-idle.

Renders draw your app's bundled images from the assets you uploaded with dart run picto:upload_assets (see Uploading Assets). An image that can't be fetched doesn't fail the render. It's left out, and the manifest lists it under warnings with its reference and a message. video and frames also print a warning: line for each on stderr. When an agent sees an empty space where it expected something, it should check warnings before deciding the app drew nothing there.

Say a user reports that checkout "sometimes does nothing". An agent with a shell can work through it like this: Find sessions where someone hammered a control that didn't respond. dart run picto:sessions list --has-rage-taps --limit 10 Read one session's timeline and find the rage tap. dart run picto:sessions timeline 3f9c2a7e The rage tap is at 1:42. Look at the screen around it. dart run picto:sessions frames 3f9c2a7e --start 1:30 --end 1:50 --every 2s -o frames/ Watch the same window as a video, with taps drawn on. dart run picto:sessions video 3f9c2a7e --start 1:30 --end 1:50 -o checkout.mp4 The timeline is often enough on its own: it shows the screen, the taps before the rage tap and, if the app records network requests, whether the request the button made came back (see What Gets Recorded).

Limits are per organization, per hour, over a sliding window, and rise with the plan: Plan Renders an hour Reads an hour Invite trial 5 300 Starter 5 300 Growth 15 1,000 Scale 30 Unlimited Enterprise 60 Unlimited A render is a timeline, video or frames request. An identical render that's already cached still counts, so reuse finished files. Every other request is a read: list, show, download, and each check on a running render. Over a limit, the request fails with rate_limited and a message naming the plan's limit and how long to wait. On every plan but Enterprise the message includes a link to your organization's billing settings. The CLI exits 1; an MCP tool returns it as the tool's error. list covers every organization you can see: one at its limit is left out and the rest are served.

The agent sees what your account sees in the dashboard: sessions from organizations you own or collaborate on that have a plan or a running invite trial. list leaves out sessions from other organizations, and opening one of them directly fails with plan_required. A session from anywhere else fails as not found. The agent never sees your API keys.

s.b: Every public item in package:picto/picto.dart, the only library a Flutter app imports, with its type and default. Each entry links to the guide that explains when to use it. import 'package:picto/picto.dart';
All members are static. There's nothing to construct.

Installs the recording binding, the error hooks and the upload queue. Call it once in main(), before runApp() and before anything else initializes a binding. It doesn't start a session. It returns the WidgetsBinding it installed. See Quick start. The signature: static WidgetsBinding setup({ required String apiKey, required String appVersion, Directory? pendingUploadsDir, int samplingPercentage = aotSamplingPercentage, Directory? samplingCacheDir, SamplingRateClient? samplingClient, Duration? maxRecordingDuration, Duration? errorWindowBefore, Duration? errorWindowAfter, Duration? backgroundTimeout, int maxNewSessionsPerHour = defaultMaxNewSessionsPerHour, }) The app below reads its key from a build define it names itself: void main() { Picto.setup( apiKey: const String.fromEnvironment('PICTO_API_KEY'), appVersion: '1.0.0', ); runApp(const MyApp()); } Parameter Type Default Meaning apiKey String Required The client app's API key (oc_...), from the dashboard. appVersion String Required Your app's version, stored on every upload. pendingUploadsDir Directory? picto_pending_uploads in an app-private directory that survives app updates Where a recording waits until it uploads. See How ses

Starts a session. Does nothing if a session is already recording, if sampling left this run out, or if the install has reached maxNewSessionsPerHour. Called within backgroundTimeout of your own endSessionAndUpload, it continues that session as its next segment. See Recording sessions. static void startRecording() For example: Picto.startRecording();

Ends the session and uploads it. Returns true only when the recording reached Picto; false covers the other three PictoSessionEndOutcome values. metadata is merged into the upload. Throws a StateError if setup was never called. See Recording sessions. static Future endSessionAndUpload({ Map<String, Object?> metadata = const {}, }) For example: final uploaded = await Picto.endSessionAndUpload();

The same call as endSessionAndUpload, returning which of the four outcomes happened. Use it when your app logs or acts on the result. See Recording sessions. static Future endSessionAndUploadOutcome({ Map<String, Object?> metadata = const {}, }) For example: final outcome = await Picto.endSessionAndUploadOutcome();

Ends the live session, uploads it and starts a new session, never a continuation. Returns the outcome of the session that ended, or nothingRecording when nothing was live (a new session still starts). Returns null and changes nothing when sampling left this run out or the install is at maxNewSessionsPerHour. metadata goes on the ending session only. Throws a StateError if setup was never called. See Recording sessions. static Future<PictoSessionEndOutcome?> restartRecording({ Map<String, Object?> metadata = const {}, }) For example: final ended = await Picto.restartRecording();

true while a session is recording, whether startRecording or an uncaught error started it. See Recording sessions. static bool get isRecording For example: if (!Picto.isRecording) Picto.startRecording();

Whether Picto's binding is the live one, so a session captures anything. Always false in a widget test, where setup stands down. See Testing. static bool get isRecordingBindingInstalled For example: expect(Picto.isRecordingBindingInstalled, isFalse);

Sends every queued recording now. You don't need to call it: Picto drains the queue during setup and when the app comes to the foreground, at most once every drainInterval. A call while a drain is running joins that drain. Does nothing in a widget test. Throws a StateError if setup was never called. See How sessions work. static Future retryPendingUploads() For example: unawaited(Picto.retryPendingUploads());

Sets a tag on the current recording. A later call with the same key replaces the value. Tags don't carry into the next session or segment. See Adding context. static void setTag(String key, String value) For example: Picto.setTag('plan', 'pro');

Names the user of the current session with your own id. It carries into every later session of the app run. See Adding context. static void identify(String userId) For example: Picto.identify('user-1234');

Puts a named event on the replay timeline at this moment. See Adding context. static void recordEvent(String name, {Map<String, String> data = const {}}) For example: Picto.recordEvent('coupon_applied', data: {'code': 'SPRING'});

Returns a new PictoNavigatorObserver on each read. Add it to navigatorObservers to record screens. See Adding context. static PictoNavigatorObserver get navigatorObserver For example: MaterialApp( navigatorObservers: [Picto.navigatorObserver], home: const HomePage(), );

Records that the user is on the screen name, for screens the Navigator never sees, such as a tab in an IndexedStack or a page of a PageView. Recording the current screen again does nothing. See Adding context. static void recordScreen(String name) For example: Picto.recordScreen('discover');
The default for setup's maxNewSessionsPerHour. static const defaultMaxNewSessionsPerHour = 30;
The shortest gap between two automatic drains of the upload queue. static const drainInterval = Duration(minutes: 5);

What ending a session did, returned by endSessionAndUploadOutcome and restartRecording. See Recording sessions. Value Meaning uploaded The recording reached Picto. The only value endSessionAndUpload reports as true. uploadFailed The upload didn't land. The recording stays queued on the device and a later drain sends it, unless Picto refused it, which the console reports with the status code. nothingRecording No session was live, so nothing was sent or queued. Not an error: backgrounding and the end of an error window both end sessions on their own. recordingPipelineAbsent Picto's binding isn't installed, so nothing was captured or sent. The session still ends. Expected in widget and integration_test runs. The switch below handles each value: switch (await Picto.endSessionAndUploadOutcome()) { case PictoSessionEndOutcome.uploaded: debugPrint('uploaded'); case PictoSessionEndOutcome.uploadFailed: debugPrint('queued, will retry'); case PictoSessionEndOutcome.nothingRecording: debugPrint('no session was live'); case PictoSessionEndOutcome.recordingPipelineAbsent: debugPrint('not recording under test'); }
Each widget changes only what's recorded beneath it. Your app draws exactly as before. See What gets recorded.

Sets whether text beneath child is captured. Text is captured by default, so enabled: false is the common use: it replaces every paragraph, icons included, with line-box placeholders. The innermost CaptureText wins. overflowPadding is the logical-pixel margin kept around each paragraph for shadows and overhang; null means a quarter of the paragraph's tallest line. It must be zero or more and finite. const CaptureText({ Key? key, required Widget child, bool enabled = true, double? overflowPadding, }) For example: CaptureText(enabled: false, child: AccountDetails());

Records the real pixels of images beneath child, within a per-session size budget, instead of placeholders. const CaptureRealImages({Key? key, required Widget child}) For example: CaptureRealImages(child: ProductPhoto());

Records an SVG, Lottie or Rive graphic beneath child as a compact raster. Wrap it tightly around the graphic. const CaptureVectorGraphics({Key? key, required Widget child}) For example: CaptureVectorGraphics(child: BrandLogo());

Records a native view, such as a map, from images it takes of itself. snapshot returns encoded image bytes, or null when there's nothing to show yet. Picto asks about once a second while the view is on screen, scales each image to 512 px on its longest edge and stops after 1 MiB per session. Nothing is captured under a text mask or ExcludeFromRecording. const CapturePlatformView({ Key? key, required Future<Uint8List?> Function() snapshot, required Widget child, }) For example: CapturePlatformView( snapshot: () async => mapController?.snapshot(), child: MapView(onCreated: (controller) => mapController = controller), );

Keeps everything beneath child out of the recording, including its position and size. const ExcludeFromRecording({Key? key, required Widget child}) For example: ExcludeFromRecording(child: PaymentForm());

An http.Client that records each request's method, URL, status code and duration. Headers and bodies are never recorded, nor is a user:password@ part of the URL. With redactQueryParameters set to true, the recorded URL also drops its query string and fragment. Requests are sent unchanged. See What gets recorded. PictoHttpClient(http.Client inner, {bool redactQueryParameters = true}) For example: final client = PictoHttpClient(http.Client());

The NavigatorObserver behind Picto.navigatorObserver, which is the usual way to get one. A screen is named by its RouteSettings.name. An unnamed route is recorded by its type, and a dialog, sheet or menu only when you name it with routeSettings. All instances share one current screen, so two can't record the same change twice. See Adding context. PictoNavigatorObserver() For example: MaterialApp(navigatorObservers: [PictoNavigatorObserver()], home: const HomePage());

A build define Picto reads: the share of app runs this build records, 100 by default. It's the default for setup's samplingPercentage and applies until the server's rate for the app arrives; a rate set in the dashboard replaces it. See Sampling. flutter build apk --dart-define=PICTO_SAMPLING_PERCENTAGE=25
